feed.title: Combined summary - [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime

entry.title: Combined summary - [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
entry.summary: The recent proposal of BIP326 marks a significant evolution in Bitcoin's transaction policies, specifically addressing the mechanisms used to combat fee sniping. This initiative involves transitioning from the exclusive use of nLockTime to a combined approach incorporating nSequence within certain taproot transactions. The draft of this Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) is available at [this GitHub repository](https://github.com/nervana21/bips/blob/anti-fee-snipe/bip-anti-fee-sniping-with-locktime.md), which also integrates existing Bitcoin Core functions like DiscourageFeeSniping and IsCurrentForAntiFeeSniping. The proposal suggests setting nLockTime to the current blockchain height with a possibility of subtracting up to 0.99% of this value, effectively preventing negative results and ensuring transaction stability. The Anti-Fee-Sniping feature brings about several considerations pertinent to user privacy and transaction security. Recent changes in Bitcoin Core have eliminated the need for BIP125 signaling, allowing transactions to be replaceable under default mempool policies without prior indicators. However, the inclusion of a 10%-back-date rule could potentially create identifiable fingerprints for transactions, raising privacy concerns. Moreover, discussions on platforms like GitHub have highlighted potential edge cases and implementation errors that could impact the efficacy and security of these transactions. For instance, incorrect implementations by specific wallets have led to identifiable transactions, although the overall impact remains minimal due to limited usage of these wallets. Furthermore, practical challenges persist in the broader adoption of Anti-Fee-Sniping measures, as evidenced by data indicating that only about 5% of transactions currently utilize a height-based time-lock ([Mainnet Observer](https://mainnet.observer/charts/transactions-height-based-locktime/)). Addressing these challenges requires careful documentation and adherence to proposed guidelines, such as those detailed in the updated BIP draft. This draft now includes explicit recommendations for documenting replacement locktime policies to facilitate a clearer understanding and better implementation practices across the Bitcoin network. These updates aim to foster a more robust framework for transaction processing, enhancing both the anonymity and efficiency of digital transactions within the Bitcoin ecosystem.
